Elon Musk announced in May 2025 that he was leaving the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), a nongovernmental task force he led to reshape federal bureaucracy by slashing government spending. He announced via his social media platform X that his "scheduled time" as a special government employee had come to an end.

Musk's role at DOGE began in January 2025 when Trump appointed him to lead efforts to streamline federal government operations, and as a "special government employee," he was legally limited to serving 130 days. After leaving DOGE, he said he would focus more on his businesses, namely SpaceX, Tesla and xAI.

In his departure announcement, Musk thanked Trump for the opportunity to reduce wasteful spending and said DOGE's mission would only strengthen over time. However, Musk indicated he would still be doing government work once or twice a week until the end of Trump's term and planned to keep his small office at the White House.
